issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] Whole-command-in-one-brace-token leak. When a delete verb and the control-plane path are leaves of the SAME brace-comma token, `__scan_one_segment_for_cp_delete()`'s verb loop matches the verb (`__verb_brace_matches` -> 0), sets `__verb_armed=1` and then `armed=1; continue`, which drops the token before the operand judge runs. [security][critical][confidence:high] The same leak survives every context in SC-11(1)'s context pool, so four-site symmetry is symmetric in the wrong direction: `$({rm,-rf,.claude,x{a..70}})` allow, `bash -c "{rm,-rf,.claude}"` allow, backtick form allow, `Q=1 {rm,-rf,.claude}` allow.

Here the undecided (`return 2`) path takes the `armed=1; continue` branch and skips the same token, so SC-10(4)'s fail-closed direction is satisfied for arming yet still fails open for the decision as a whole.

[security][high][confidence:high] `{find,.claude,-delete,-o,-name,<600 A>}` -> allow + real deletion. Both find/-delete flags come from the same undecided token, so the new `__find_src -eq $__delete_src` exception suppresses arming. The rule's stated rationale ('one word cannot be both the command and its predicate') is false for brace expansion, which turns one word into many. Pre-existing allow at 00e105e (the `x{a..70}` sibling is ask at both commits), so this is not a regression, but it is an unattributed allow cell inside the axis.

[test][high][confidence:high] The generator in tests/pre-bash-firewall-generated.bats builds each cell by inserting one construct into the i-th character of the target WORD and always leaves the operand as a separate word (`template_for` -> `%s -rf .claude`). By construction it can never emit a cell where the construct's expansion supplies both the verb and the operand. SC-11(2) says the product must be enumerated by code rather than by hand, but the code's own enumeration rule contains the same blind spot the hand-written 66-cell corpus had; the axis is generated along the construct dimension only, not along 'what the expansion is allowed to contain'.

[test][medium][confidence:high] Friction control group (generated test 10) covers the false-positive direction of the self-fix but has no cell where a brace token carries a control-plane path, so the leak has no counterpart assertion in either suite.

[error][medium][confidence:medium] `__verb_brace_matches_impl()`'s 512-char guard fires before it even looks for `{`, so ANY token longer than 512 characters returns 2 from the brace-verb call site and provisionally arms the segment. Combined with a control-plane operand this asks on unrelated commands (`jq '<600-char program>' .claude/settings.json`). Direction is safe and consistent with SC-10(4); recording it as measured friction rather than a defect.

[quality][low][confidence:high] `_residual_risk_AC11.open_axes_2026_08_04.ancestor_directory_operand` is now stale in the safe direction: its two named examples `rm -rf hooks` and `find hooks -delete` both measure ask at 21889d0, yet the key still describes them as allow and the generated suite would accept an allow there. [quality][low][confidence:medium] `D=-delete find .claude $D` (assignment as a command prefix rather than a separate segment) is allow. In bash the prefix assignment is not visible to the expansion of `$D` in the same command, so the command degrades to `find .claude` and nothing is deleted; reporting it only because it sits adjacent to the assignment axis step 15 wired and the safe behavior here is incidental to shell semantics, not to a check.

[quality][low][confidence:high] The INV-15 appendix added in docs/INVARIANTS.md states the axis was defined by a generation rule; given the above it overstates coverage in the same way the criterion warns against. It should name the generator's own scope limit (constructs are inserted into a word, operands stay separate words).

missing_criteria: SC-11(1) enumerates the constructs and the contexts but never says what the construct's expansion may CONTAIN. Because every past round inserted a construct into a word and kept the operand separate, 'brace-comma at the verb position' has silently meant 'brace-comma that expands to the verb and nothing else'. The axis needs a fourth dimension — expansion payload: {verb only, verb + harmless extra words, verb + the control-plane operand, verb + operand + padding} — otherwise the generator reproduces the blind spot it was created to remove.

No criterion states the invariant that actually broke here: a token consumed as a verb must still be examined as an operand when its expansion yields more than one word. 'Consumed as verb' and 'skipped as operand' are treated as the same act throughout scan_control_plane_delete().
ambiguous_criteria: SC-11(3) says a deferral is fail-closed only when a downstream judge covers the position, but scopes itself to `__verb_brace_matches()`'s return 1/2. The same reasoning applies to any `continue` that ends a token's judgment; the criterion should be phrased over 'checks that terminate a token's judgment' rather than over the tri-state return.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-10(7) attribution is only enforced where a test asserts allow. The leaking cells are simply absent from both suites, so nothing forced the attribution question to be asked. Attribution needs to be driven by a generator that covers the axis, which loops back to the missing expansion-payload dimension.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Extend SC-11(1) with the expansion-payload dimension and re-generate; fix the operand-skip at both the rc=0 and rc=2 branches of the verb loop (arming a token must not exempt it from the operand judge when the token contains a brace/substitution that yields multiple words); drop or narrow the `__find_src -eq $__delete_src` exception; refresh the ancestor_directory_operand residual to match measured behavior.

recommended_fix.primary: In the verb loop of `__scan_one_segment_for_cp_delete()`, stop coupling 'this token armed the segment' to 'this token is not an operand'. When the matched/undecided token contains `{`, `$(`, backtick or `${`, arm and then still run the operand judge on it (the brace operand judge `__control_plane_location_impl()` already expands the same leaves, so `{rm,-rf,.claude}` would find `.claude`). The AUDIT-6 self-fix regression the `continue` was protecting (`cp file{1..300} /tmp/`, `rm -rf x{1..999}`) is about a token whose leaves are NOT control-plane paths, so running the operand judge does not reintroduce it — the control cells in generated test 10 pin that.
recommended_fix.secondary: Replace the `__find_src -eq $__delete_src` exception with a check on whether the token can expand to more than one word; only a single-word token can be excluded on the 'one word cannot be both' argument.
recommended_fix.then: Add the expansion-payload dimension to the generator and re-run; every new allow cell must be attributed before the suite is allowed to skip it.
